remainingLimitations: Discrete toy workload with deterministic A-first ties; Envoy least-request samples candidates and breaks ties differently. Not a benchmark.
Real balancers usually cannot observe remaining work at all; the side view is the reader’s privilege, not a proposed routing signal.
A strictly top-down perspective view still shows slightly larger tops for taller columns, and the host key light casts shadows whose length hints at height.
A 2D chart could show the same counts and heights side by side; the 3D contribution is the perspective comparison itself. Policy comparison (round robin vs least request) is left to the video.
Coordinator browser QA of 420px framing of both views is outstanding.
recommendationRationale: The perspective toggle carries a substantive spatial mechanism (the routing signal is a projection that drops remaining work) at a decision the video never reaches. The benefit is moderate; the coordinator should reject it if the 420px top view does not make the two lanes read as alike.
